statements: My first action in this task was to run git -C on the Cobra checkout and confirm HEAD printed exactly a0a6ae020bb3899ff0276067863e50523f897370; I opened no file in that tree before that check returned.

I ran no retrieval of any kind: no graphi CLI, no mcp__graphi__* tool, no task_context, no semantic or lexical search engine. I never saw a ranked list, a relevance score, a bundle, a saved hit list, a retrieval metric or a trace. My only search was plain grep and git grep inside the pinned checkout.

I made no GitHub request and no web request. I used no gh, no WebFetch, no WebSearch and no browser. I read no issue body, no issue comment, no label, no linked pull request and nothing a maintainer wrote; the sealed Q text in batch-5-input.jsonl was the whole of what I knew about each report.

The only repository I read was the pinned Cobra checkout at <cobra-checkout>. I did not read graphi's own source, its datasets, its tests, or any harvest directory other than the three files my task named.

Beyond those three files, the only file outside the pinned checkout that I read is my own output file annotations-5.jsonl, which I re-read solely to verify its JSON, its issue ordering and its anchors. I record this rather than omit it.

Every anchor I cite occurs inside its cited inclusive line range at the pin. I verified all 58 spans twice: once by reading the byte range directly, and once by re-extracting each range with sed -n START,ENDp and confirming the anchor substring is present. Both passes reported zero failures.
Every cited path is a tracked file at the pin, confirmed against git ls-files, and every answerable row carries at least one grade-3 span in a tracked, regular .go file.

No verdict of mine was decided by how long a search took, by how many files I had to open, by how deep an answer sat in a call chain, by identifier overlap, or by any expectation about how a retrieval system would perform on the question. I applied no time budget and no file-count budget.

I did not rewrite any sealed rubric, did not add bespoke expected-answer wording to any rubric, and did not change any answer mode. Where a sealed question was ambiguous I recorded the ambiguity in the row's note rather than narrowing or restating the question.
Both not_answerable rows name a disqualifier and give positive, cited evidence for it in the note; neither rests on failure to find something.

I returned no unresolved rows. Each of the 18 candidates finished with either reviewed grade-3 evidence satisfying A1-A4 or a positive D-clause finding, and I did not use unresolved as a substitute for either.

I ran two short Python verification scripts from a scratchpad directory. They executed only git rev-parse, git ls-files, sed and local file reads against the pinned checkout and my own output file; they performed no search, ranking, scoring or network access.
